verification.funding_note: No cash stipend is published. The KIIT International Scholarship (KUISP) is a tuition waiver: two students and ten students from each country receive full and half tuition fee waivers respectively, with a total of 100 scholarships available.
verification.covered_expenses: Tuition fee waivers only (full waiver for 2 students per country, half waiver for 10 students per country). No monthly stipend, housing, food, insurance or travel component is published.
verification.degree_level: B.Tech, M.Tech, MCA, MBA, LLB and PhD programmes for international students
eligibility: Foreign national and NRI applicants applying through KIIT's international admissions portal
Awards are allocated per country: 2 full and 10 half tuition waivers per country, 100 scholarships in total
required_docs: Academic transcripts and certificates from previous institutions
Proof of English proficiency (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS) if applicable - not compulsory
English-translated documents if the applicant is from a non-English-speaking country
verification.application_process: Register on international.kiit.ac.in, verify the registered email, click Apply Now, complete the programme/personal, address, educational qualification, upload and declaration sections, and submit. The admissions team processes the application and releases an offer letter, which is downloadable from the student dashboard; acceptance is then confirmed and the student visa prepared through KIIT's International Relations Office.
verification.contact_info: International Relations Office, Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT), Patia, Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751024, India; internationaloffice@kiit.ac.in; +91-9354030108
verification.english_test_requirement: No compulsory English test. Proof of English proficiency (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS) is required only 'if applicable' and is explicitly not compulsory.
verification.documented_student_count: 100 scholarships total (2 full and 10 half tuition waivers per country)
verification.status_note: KIIT's main website blocks automated access (HTTP 403), so scholarship details were verified from the official 'Scholarships and Fellowships' page snapshot of 23 August 2026 (archived copy of kiit.ac.in/scholarships-fellowships) and the official international admissions pages international.kiit.ac.in and the archived KiIT study-at-KIIT page, all retrieved 2026-10-10. The instruction that the quantum and period of scholarship are subject to change appears on KIIT's page, so reconfirm current terms with the International Relations Office.

applicant_utility.exciting_but_honest_wins: A per-country quota is the unusual thing here: two students from your country get a full tuition waiver and another ten get a half waiver, out of 100 awards in total. That means you compete mostly against your own compatriots for a fee waiver at a large private university, and the waiver applies across engineering, management, law and doctoral programmes. The application itself is light - no entrance exam, no interview - and admission runs through a single portal that issues an offer letter you can download from your dashboard.
applicant_utility.good_fit_if: You want a full English-medium degree in India without an entrance exam, you can cover living costs and any remaining fees yourself, and your home country is one where the two-seat and ten-seat quotas still have room. It suits applicants from countries underrepresented in Indian universities, because your main competition is your own cohort rather than the whole applicant pool.
applicant_utility.potential_drawbacks: The award is tuition-only: there is no stipend, no housing or food support, no insurance and no airfare, so a full waiver still leaves a real budget gap in Bhubaneswar. With a hundred seats shared across dozens of countries, the per-country slots are few and are awarded on rolling admissions, and KIIT itself notes that the quantum and period of scholarship can change. Anything beyond tuition - lab, exam and hostel fees - remains yours to pay.
document_checklist: All secondary and tertiary transcripts and certificates
Certified English translations of non-English documents
TOEFL or IELTS certificate only if you already have one
Registration and email verification on international.kiit.ac.in, then submit before offer letters for the academic year run out
applicant_utility.playbook_for_working_applicants: Register on the KIIT international portal as early as you can: admissions are processed into rolling offer letters, so the award pool for your country shrinks as the year advances. Email internationaloffice@kiit.ac.in with your name, country and intended programme to ask how many of your country's two full and ten half waivers remain before you commit. Frame your academics around a clear programme choice rather than a general interest, and line up a realistic budget for fees beyond tuition plus roughly a year of living costs, since the waiver will not touch them. Once the offer letter arrives, confirm enrollment promptly and let the International Relations Office handle the bonafide needed for your student visa appointment.
